title: Reference: 200 ms windows, 95 % overlap, shuffled, state reset · per-angle scaling
description: Earlier round: the reference with per-angle loss scaling (each angle's torque target divided by its training spread), before the scaling was removed (13 Nov 2026). Kept for comparison. The setting every other entry of this study changes in exactly one way: 20 steps of 10 ms (200 ms), a new window every 10 ms (95 % overlap), windows shuffled every epoch, LSTM state reset at every window. Everything else as the reference: Active torque (each session's own relaxed-hold passive torque subtracted), EMG ÷ session-1 maximum, per-angle loss scaling, LSTM 8×2 trained with batch 64 (fast protocol: learning rate × 0.5 after 6 flat epochs, early stop 15, at most 150 epochs), trained on session 1 and tested on session 2, 6 people × 10 seeds. The EMG envelope is causal (forward-only filters: no input uses later EMG, as in a real-time device; 2nd-order 2 Hz low-pass, about 125 ms lag) and the first and last 1 s of every trial are cut. Validation windows start one window span after the training part of each trial, so no validation window reuses training inputs (purged split).
